docs.title: InstaGene
docs.text: A suite of tools for reading, editing, and constructing nucleic acid and protein sequences, built as a reusable engine with three independent front-ends.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Desktop GUICLIWeb

Install the Linux .deb and open files from the terminal:

sudo apt install ./instagene_0.0.3_amd64.deb
instagene plasmid.gb

Or run the portable JAR (Java 21+):

java -Xmx8g -jar instagene-gui.jar

Build from source and inspect a sequence:

./gradlew :app-cli:runCli --args="info sequence.gb"
./gradlew :app-cli:runCli --args="digest --enzyme EcoRI sequence.gb"

Start the embedded web server:

./gradlew :app-web:runWeb --args="--port 8080"

Open http://localhost:8080 in your browser.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Module Description Run with engine Reusable core library (org.instagene.core) dependency app-cli Command-line tool, scriptable ./gradlew :app-cli:runCli app-gui Desktop front-end (Swing + FlatLaf) ./gradlew :app-gui:runGui app-web Web interface (embedded HTTP server) ./gradlew :app-web:runWeb tests Cross-module integration test suite ./gradlew test

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Sequence I/O — FASTA, GenBank, and plain-text formats
  • Restriction mapping — enzyme catalog, CpG methylation analysis, virtual gel
  • Alignment — Needleman-Wunsch with affine gap penalties, Sanger read alignment
  • Primer design — melting temperature, thermodynamic screening, primer design
  • CRISPR — Ruleset 3 guide RNA scoring and PAM site detection
  • ORF finding — all six reading frames, customizable codon tables
  • Plasmid construction — Golden Gate, Gibson assembly, recombination
  • Genome statistics — GC content, CpG islands, Shannon entropy, tandem repeats
  • Theming — runtime theme discovery from all installed FlatLaf themes

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Pre-built installers are available from the GitHub Releases page:

Platform Format Notes Linux .deb Ubuntu/Debian, includes /usr/bin/instagene wrapper Linux .rpm Fedora/RHEL Linux App image zip Portable, no install required Windows .msi WiX-based installer Any GUI JAR java -Xmx8g -jar instagene-gui.jar Any CLI zip instagene-cli.zip with launcher script

docs.title: Using the Engine Library
docs.text:
The engine is published to GitHub Packages as org.instagene:instagene-engine. Add it to your project:

repositories {
    maven {
        url = uri("https://maven.pkg.github.com/novelprotein/instagene")
        credentials {
            username = System.getenv("GITHUB_ACTOR")
            password = System.getenv("GITHUB_TOKEN")
        }
    }
}

dependencies {
    implementation("org.instagene:instagene-engine:0.0.3")
}

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: The command-line interface (app-cli) provides scriptable access to all engine features. Run instagene help for the full command list.

docs.title: Global Options
docs.text: Option Description --env FILE Load defaults from a KEY=VALUE environment file --no-colors Disable ANSI color output

docs.title: info
docs.text:
Display sequence metadata: name, length, topology, base composition, GC content.

instagene info sequence.gb
instagene info --format fasta sequence.txt

docs.title: gc
docs.text:
Compute GC content, GC skew profile, and cumulative GC skew.

instagene gc sequence.gb
instagene gc --window 500 sequence.gb

docs.title: orf
docs.text:
Find open reading frames in all reading frames.

instagene orf --min-aa 30 sequence.gb
instagene orf --table STANDARD --both-strands sequence.gb

docs.title: find
docs.text:
Search for a degenerate or literal pattern on one or both strands.

instagene find --pattern "ATCGNR" sequence.gb
instagene find --pattern "MVLSPADK" --mode amino-acid protein.fa

docs.title: align
docs.text:
Align multiple sequences using Needleman-Wunsch with affine gap penalties.

instagene align reference.gb query1.gb query2.gb

docs.title: identity
docs.text:
Compute pairwise sequence identity between aligned sequences.

instagene identity aligned.fa

docs.title: digest
docs.text:
Perform restriction enzyme digestion and display fragments.

instagene digest --enzyme EcoRI sequence.gb
instagene digest --enzymes EcoRI,HindIII,BamHI sequence.gb

docs.title: sites
docs.text:
Show all recognition sites for one or more enzymes.

instagene sites --enzyme EcoRI sequence.gb
instagene sites --enzymes ALL --unique sequence.gb

docs.title: enzymes
docs.text:
Analyze enzyme cutting frequency across the full catalog.

instagene enzymes --times 1 sequence.gb

docs.title: gel
docs.text:
Simulate a restriction digest gel electrophoresis.

instagene gel --enzyme EcoRI --ladder ladder.gb sequence.gb

docs.title: revcomp
docs.text:
Reverse complement a sequence.

instagene revcomp sequence.gb

docs.title: complement
docs.text:
Complement a sequence.

instagene complement sequence.gb

docs.title: transcribe
docs.text:
Transcribe DNA to RNA.

instagene transcribe sequence.gb

docs.title: translate
docs.text:
Translate nucleotide sequence to protein.

instagene translate --table STANDARD sequence.gb

docs.title: annotate
docs.text:
Annotate features on a sequence.

instagene annotate --region 100..500 --label "Promoter" sequence.gb

docs.title: plasmid
docs.text:
Design a circular plasmid map.

instagene plasmid --backbone backbone.gb --insert insert.gb

docs.title: gibson
docs.text:
Design a Gibson assembly.

instagene gibson --fragments frag1.gb,frag2.gb,frag3.gb

docs.title: golden-gate
docs.text:
Design a Golden Gate assembly.

instagene golden-gate --enzyme BsaI --fragments frag1.gb,frag2.gb

docs.title: primers
docs.text:
Design primers for PCR amplification.

instagene primers --target region.gb --tm 60

docs.title: tm
docs.text:
Compute melting temperature using nearest-neighbor thermodynamics.

instagene tm "ATCGATCGATCG"

docs.title: screen
docs.text:
Full primer screening: hairpin, self-dimer, cross-dimer, delta-G stability.

instagene screen "ATCGATCGATCG"

docs.title: bench
docs.text:
Run built-in performance benchmarks.

instagene bench                    # use built-in test sequence
instagene bench sequence.gb        # benchmark with your sequence

See the Benchmarks page for historical performance data.

docs.title: Development Setup
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository: 

    git clone https://github.com/novelprotein/instagene.git
cd instagene

  2. Install git hooks: 

    ./scripts/install-hooks.sh

  3. Build and test: 

    ./gradlew build

docs.title: Architecture Rules
docs.text:
The project enforces strict separation between the engine and front-ends:

  • Engine (engine/) must never reference org.instagene.app
  • Front-ends must never reference each other
  • The published engine jar must contain only core classes

Run ./gradlew verifySeparation to check these rules.

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text:
./gradlew test                   # all tests
./gradlew :tests:test            # cross-module tests only
./gradlew :engine:test           # engine tests only

docs.title: Adding Tests
docs.text: Every bug fix should include a regression test. Tests live in the tests module under tests/src/test/kotlin/. Shared test utilities are in tests/src/test/kotlin/org/instagene/TestHelpers.kt.

docs.title: Code Style
docs.text:
• Kotlin with no comments unless complex logic requires explanation
  • No wildcard imports
  • Functions that do heavy computation should consider the Parallel utility for parallelization

docs.title: Pull Requests
docs.text:
1. Create a feature branch from master
  2. Make your changes and ensure ./gradlew build passes
  3. Open a pull request against master
  4. CI will run the full test suite automatically

docs.title: Benchmarks
docs.text:
Performance benchmarks run on every push to master. The benchmark suite is opt-in via -Dinstagene.perf=true and requires a sequence file as input:

./gradlew :app-cli:bench -Dinstagene.perf=true -Pinput=sequence.fa

Results are published to the Benchmarks dashboard.

docs.title: Engine API
docs.text: The engine (org.instagene.core) is a pure Kotlin library with no UI dependencies. It provides the core bioinformatics operations used by all front-ends.

docs.title: Module
docs.text:
dependencies {
    implementation("org.instagene:instagene-engine:0.0.3")
}

docs.title: Package Structure
docs.text:
org.instagene.core
├── Sequence I/O
│   ├── Seq                    # Core sequence model
│   ├── FastaReader            # FASTA format parser
│   ├── GenBankReader          # GenBank format parser
│   └── ChromatogramReader     # AB1/FSC chromatogram parser
├── Analysis
│   ├── SequenceStatistics     # GC content, entropy, CpG islands
│   ├── Digest                 # Restriction enzyme mapping
│   ├── Alignment              # Needleman-Wunsch alignment
│   ├── SangerAlignment        # Sanger read alignment
│   └── FeatureLibrary         # Feature annotation and search
├── Design
│   ├── PrimerThermodynamics   # Melting temperature, hairpin, dimer
│   ├── PrimerDesign           # Primer design with Tm targeting
│   ├── CrisprDesign           # CRISPR guide RNA design (Ruleset 3)
│   └── SiteDomestication      # Restriction site removal
├── Assembly
│   ├── Assembly               # Fragment assembly and overlap
│   ├── Recombination          # Homologous recombination
│   └── VirtualGel             # Gel electrophoresis simulation
└── Utilities
    ├── Alphabet               # IUPAC codes, complements, translations
    ├── CodonTable             # Codon translation tables
    ├── Enzymes                # Restriction enzyme catalog
    └── Parallel               # Coroutine-based parallel computation

docs.title: Seq
docs.text:
The core sequence data class:

data class Seq(
    val name: String,
    val bases: String,
    val kind: SeqKind,          // DNA, RNA, PROTEIN
    val topology: Topology,     // LINEAR, CIRCULAR
    val features: List<Feature>,
)

docs.title: Digest
docs.text:
Restriction enzyme mapping:

// Count cut sites for all enzymes
val counts = Digest.cutCounts(seq)

// Find all cut sites for specific enzymes
val sites = Digest.cutSites(seq, listOf(Enzymes.ECORI, Enzymes.HINDIII))

// Find enzymes that cut exactly once
val unique = Digest.enzymesCutting(seq, times = 1)

docs.title: SequenceStatistics
docs.text:
Genome statistics:

val gc = SequenceStatistics.gcContent(seq)
val islands = SequenceStatistics.cpgIslands(seq)
val entropy = SequenceStatistics.computeStats(seq).shannonEntropy

docs.title: Alignment
docs.text:
Multiple sequence alignment:

val result = Alignment.align(reference, queries)
val discrepancies = result.discrepancyPositions()

docs.title: PrimerThermodynamics
docs.text:
Primer analysis:

val tm = PrimerThermodynamics.meltingTemp(primer)
val hairpin = PrimerThermodynamics.assessHairpin(primer)
val selfDimer = PrimerThermodynamics.assessSelfDimer(primer)

docs.title: Parallelization
docs.text:
The engine uses kotlinx.coroutines for CPU-bound parallel computation via the Parallel utility class. Methods that iterate over large enzyme catalogs or process multiple sequences are automatically parallelized when the input size exceeds a threshold.

Key parallelized operations:

  • Digest.cutCounts / cutSites — parallel over enzymes
  • Alignment.align — parallel over query sequences
  • FeatureLibrary.previewMatches — parallel over feature definitions
  • SequenceStatistics.cpgIslands — parallel over window positions
  • AdvancedSearch.find — parallel over strands

docs.title: Thread Safety
docs.text: All engine methods are stateless and thread-safe. The Parallel utility uses Dispatchers.Default for CPU-bound work and does not maintain shared state between coroutines.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Java 21 or newer (for building from source)
  • Gradle (via the included wrapper ./gradlew)

docs.title: Building from Source
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/novelprotein/instagene.git
cd instagene
./gradlew build

This compiles all modules and runs the full test suite.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
Desktop GUICLIWeb 
./gradlew run                              # default front-end
./gradlew :app-gui:runGui                  # explicit

./gradlew :app-cli:runCli --args="help"    # list all commands
./gradlew :app-cli:runCli --args="info sequence.gb"

./gradlew :app-web:runWeb --args="--port 8080"

docs.title: Opening Files
docs.text:
The GUI and CLI accept sequence files directly:

# GUI: open files in the editor
./gradlew :app-gui:runGui --args="plasmid.gb genes.fasta"

# CLI: inspect a sequence
./gradlew :app-cli:runCli --args="info plasmid.gb"

docs.title: Supported Formats
docs.text: Format Extension Notes FASTA .fa, .fasta, .fna, .faa Nucleotide or protein GenBank .gb, .gbk, .genbank Features, annotations, topology Plain .txt, .seq Raw sequence text

docs.title: Gradle Tasks Reference
docs.text: Task Description ./gradlew run Run the default front-end (GUI) ./gradlew build Build and test everything ./gradlew check Run all checks including tests ./gradlew :app-cli:runCli Run the CLI ./gradlew :app-gui:runGui Run the desktop GUI ./gradlew :app-web:runWeb Run the web server ./gradlew :app-cli:bench Run performance benchmarks

docs.title: GUI Reference
docs.text: The desktop GUI (app-gui) is a Swing application with FlatLaf theming. It provides a visual interface for editing, analyzing, and constructing sequences.

docs.title: Launching
docs.text:
./gradlew :app-gui:runGui                           # from source
java -Xmx8g -jar instagene-gui.jar                  # portable JAR
instagene gui sequence.gb                            # via CLI launcher

docs.title: File
docs.text:
• Open — Load a sequence file (FASTA, GenBank, plain text)
  • Save / Save As — Export the current sequence
  • Recent Files — Quick access to recently opened files
  • Exit — Close the application

docs.title: Edit
docs.text:
• Undo / Redo — Full edit history with unlimited undo
  • Cut / Copy / Paste — Standard clipboard operations
  • Select All — Select the entire sequence

docs.title: View
docs.text:
• Zoom In / Out — Adjust sequence display size
  • Wrap Lines — Toggle line wrapping in the sequence view

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
• Restriction Digest — Interactive enzyme selection and fragment display
  • ORF Finder — Find open reading frames with configurable parameters
  • Primer Design — Design and screen primers with thermodynamic analysis
  • Alignment — Align sequences with Needleman-Wunsch
  • CpG Analysis — Detect CpG islands and methylation patterns
  • CRISPR Design — Guide RNA design with Ruleset 3 scoring

docs.title: Graph
docs.text:
Generate publication-quality charts:

Chart Description GC Content Sliding-window GC percentage GC Skew G-C skew profile Cumulative GC Skew Cumulative skew showing replication origins Melting Temperature Per-position Tm profile CpG Density Observed/expected CpG ratio per window CpG Islands Island detection with configurable parameters

docs.title: Theme
docs.text: Switch between installed FlatLaf themes at runtime. All IntelliJ themes installed on the system are automatically discovered.

docs.title: Sequence View
docs.text:
Displays the nucleotide or amino acid sequence with syntax highlighting:

  • DNA — A (green), T (red), G (yellow), C (blue)
  • RNA — A, U, G, C with same coloring
  • Protein — Amino acids colored by chemistry

docs.title: Annotation Panel
docs.text: Shows annotated features (CDS, gene, promoter, etc.) with position, type, and strand information. Features are draggable for reordering.

docs.title: Analysis Panel
docs.text: Orchestrates analysis tools. Each analysis runs in a background thread (SwingWorker) to keep the UI responsive during computation.

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text: Shortcut Action Ctrl+O Open file Ctrl+S Save Ctrl+Z Undo Ctrl+Shift+Z Redo Ctrl+Plus Zoom in Ctrl+Minus Zoom out

docs.title: Theming
docs.text: The GUI uses FlatLaf for native-looking UI on all platforms. Themes are discovered at runtime by scanning the classpath for FlatLaf theme classes. All IntelliJ IDEA themes bundled with flatlaf-intellij-themes are available out of the box.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
The GUI uses multi-threaded computation:

  • Analysis tasks run in SwingWorker background threads
  • Chart updates are dispatched on the EDT
  • Engine parallelism uses coroutines for CPU-bound operations

docs.title: Benchmarks
docs.text: InstaGene includes a built-in performance benchmark suite that tracks execution time across all major engine operations.

docs.title: Running Benchmarks
docs.text:
# Run with the built-in test sequence
./gradlew :app-cli:bench

# Run with your own sequence
./gradlew :app-cli:bench -Pinput=sequence.fa

Benchmarks require the instagene.perf=true system property (set automatically when using the bench task). Each operation is measured 3 times and the minimum time is reported.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
The interactive benchmark dashboard is hosted on GitHub Pages and shows historical performance trends:

View Benchmark Dashboard

The dashboard is automatically updated on every push to master via the CI workflow.

docs.title: What Is Measured
docs.text: Category Operations Sequence I/O FASTA read/write, GenBank read/write Digest Single enzyme, full catalog (48 enzymes) Alignment Pairwise NW, multiple query alignment Statistics GC content, CpG islands, Shannon entropy Search Forward/reverse pattern search, amino acid search Translation Codon table translation, ORF finding Primer Melting temperature, hairpin assessment, self-dimer

docs.title: Interpreting Results
docs.text:
• ms — milliseconds (lower is better)
  • Regression flag — operations that slow down by >15% are flagged
  • Baseline comparison — each run is compared against the previous commit
